biggest_catch: Hacker News provides zero payment protection: every dollar depends on a deal you negotiate yourself with a stranger, with no escrow and no dispute process.
catches: HN publishes no rates; pay is whatever you negotiate privately with each poster, and many posters expect bargain rates.
No escrow or payment protection — non-payment risk is entirely on you; always agree on terms and payment method before starting work.
The monthly thread is highly competitive: hundreds of freelancer replies compete for each client post.
Posters are anonymous internet strangers; verify identity and legitimacy before doing work or sharing personal details.
HN's own guidelines say 'don't use HN primarily for promotion' — drive-by spam pitches get flagged and kill your reputation.
Nothing is guaranteed: replying to the thread does not guarantee any client contact, let alone paid work.

steps: Create a free Hacker News account (news.ycombinator.com).
On the 1st of each month, open the monthly 'Freelancer? Seeking freelancer?' thread posted by whoishiring.
Read the 'seeking freelancer' client posts for work matching your skills (dev, design, writing, etc.).
Reply in-thread to a client post with your skills, rate, portfolio link, and contact details.
Negotiate scope, rate, and payment method privately with the client before starting any work.
timing: The freelancer thread is posted on the 1st of each month and accepts replies all month; project timing and pay schedule are negotiated per client.
